rationales: Cl₂ and O₂ have nonpolar bonds because each bond joins identical atoms.
N₂ has a nonpolar bond, while H₂O has polar bonds.
C₃H₈ is generally treated as nonpolar, while H₂O has polar bonds.
HCl and H₂O both contain polar covalent bonds.
Groups 1 and 2 are in the s-block because their outermost electrons occupy s subshells.
The p-block contains groups 13 to 18.
The d-block contains the transition elements.
The f-block contains the inner-transition elements.
A beta particle is an electron or positron, not a helium nucleus.
A helium-4 nucleus with a 2+ charge is an alpha particle.
A gamma particle is electromagnetic radiation, not a helium nucleus.
A helium nucleus is positively charged, so it is not neutral.
Iodine is a lustrous non-metal.
Phosphorus is not characteristically lustrous.
Sulphur is generally dull rather than lustrous.
Hydrogen is a gas and is not lustrous.
A triple bond does not involve eight shared electrons.
A triple covalent bond consists of three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Four electrons make two shared pairs, corresponding to a double bond.
Three electrons cannot make three shared pairs in a triple bond.
V/m means volume of solute per mass of solution, not grams per 100 cm³.
V/v means volume of solute per volume of solution.
M/v means mass of solute per volume of solution, as in grams per 100 cm³.
M/m means mass of solute per mass of solution.
Cations are positively charged ions, not shared electron pairs.
Anions are negatively charged ions, not shared electron pairs.
A bond pair is a pair of electrons shared to form a chemical bond.
A lone pair is a pair of valence electrons not shared in a bond.
Zinc is not the metal typically noted for fine jewelry.
Sodium is highly reactive and unsuitable for jewelry items.
Platinum is durable, lustrous, and valued for making jewelry.
Lead is soft and toxic, so it is unsuitable for jewelry.
Z commonly denotes atomic number.
P can denote the number of protons, but not the mass number.
n denotes the number of neutrons, not the mass number.
A is the conventional symbol for mass number.
Rutherford is widely regarded as the father of nuclear science.
Bohr is known for his atomic model, not as the father of nuclear science.
Newton is known for classical mechanics, not nuclear science.
Dalton is known for atomic theory, not as the father of nuclear science.
Atomic radius generally increases, rather than decreases, from right to left across a period.
Ionization energy generally decreases from right to left across a period.
Electron affinity generally decreases from right to left across a period in the simplified periodic trend taught at this level.
Electronegativity generally decreases from right to left across a period; therefore, three listed properties fit and the question has no unique answer.
The s subshell is filled across the s-block, not groups 13 to 18.
The valence electrons of groups 13 to 18 generally occupy p subshells.
The d subshell is associated mainly with the transition elements.
The f subshell is associated with the inner-transition elements.
An ionic bond forms through electron transfer and electrostatic attraction.
A covalent bond forms through mutual sharing of valence electrons.
A metallic bond involves attraction between metal ions and delocalized electrons.
A coordinate covalent bond is formed when one atom supplies both electrons in a shared pair.
Percentage is one way to express the proportion of solute, but it is not the general term.
Concentration describes the proportion of solute in a solution.
Molarity is a specific concentration measure in moles per litre.
Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves under specified conditions.
H₂ is diatomic, so it is not a triatomic molecule.
O₃ contains three atoms and is triatomic.
H₂O contains three atoms and is triatomic.
CO₂ contains three atoms and is triatomic.
